newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker as U.S. market softens.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker as U.S. market softens.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended weaker on Thursday, softening along with U.S. Treasuries amid strong U.S. economic data the lingering effect of Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's hawkish public testimony, analysts said.

"We saw quite a bit of curve flattening going on (earlier), but when the U.S. deteriorated at midday, our whole market just deteriorated with them including long bonds," said Will Sutherland, vice-president of fixed-income with Altamira Investment Services.
Canada's 30-year bond fell C$0.45 to C$111.05 to yield 7.067 percent.
The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond fell 14/32 to yield 6.81 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds was 26 basis points at Wednesday's close.
Canadian and U.S. fixed-income prices tumbled on Wednesday after Greenspan testified to the U.S. Congress that a pre-emptive interest rate hike aimed at controlling inflation could not be ruled out.
Both markets extended losses this morning as stronger-than-expected U.S. durable goods orders data added to concern about a possible rate rise in the near term in the United States, analysts said.

Sutherland said Greenspan's comments raised the question of how the Bank of Canada of would respond to a rate hike by the Fed. As a result many investors moved further up the yield curve early in the session.
In new issue news, the Government of Canada plans to auction on March 5 C$500 million of real return bonds with a coupon of 4.25 percent and maturing on December 1, 2026.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.32 to C$104.08 to yield 6.428 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 9/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 14 basis points from 15 basis points at Wednesday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.92 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.21 percent.
